title: My dragon companion now hatches after 60 kills
author: MythpipGames
selftext:
The Dragon Tamer's companion, Pip, used to be an egg that just floated next to you and hatched at the end of wave 1, no matter what you did. It felt like nothing.

Now every kill adds a few more cracks, and after 60 kills Pip hatches mid-fight. So the egg is now a tiny progress bar you can actually see.

How the AI part actually works for me: I describe what I want in plain words (in German, actually), Claude writes the GDScript, and I test it on my phone and decide if it feels right. The biggest problem was that AI changes sometimes quietly break something else. So Claude also wrote a bot that replays runs with a fixed seed. I compare runs before and after a change, and this clip was recorded by that same bot.

For Pip, the idea was mine (the egg felt pointless). Claude built the crack stages and the hatch, and it took a few rounds until the timing felt right.

Two questions: does the hatch read well enough on a phone, or does it need a bigger pop? And for those of you building with AI: how do you catch changes that break something unrelated?

comments.author: MythpipGames
comments.body: The closed beta just opened on Android – if you want to see Pip hatch on your own phone, everything's on Discord: [https://discord.gg/6cHXQZ3rmh](https://discord.gg/6cHXQZ3rmh)

comments.author: TailorGame
comments.body: Turning the egg into a visible kill counter is a good fix, since it gives a passive companion a reason to be watched. The fixed-seed replay bot is the smartest part of your workflow, because comparing runs before and after a change is exactly how you catch the quiet regressions AI edits cause. For the hatch timing, I'd try making the last few cracks escalate (a shake or sound) around kill 50 so the mid-fight hatch feels earned rather than abrupt.

replies.author: MythpipGames
replies.body: Thanks, building up the last few cracks sounds worth testing. A small shake before the hatch could make the progress clearer without making the whole effect bigger.
